system.biography: Acolytes are beginning spellcasters that draw their power from the gods. Due to the popularity and strength of Kari, the human goddess, the vast majority of acolyte’s in the world are human. However, acolytes of other races do still exist. Some may follow Kari, while others may follow their own god or goddess.

details.appearance: Varies
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics: Acolytes serve as frontliners that can heal themselves or allies. Cure Touch can be used immediately when an ally drops low enough to gain the full benefit from it. Acolytes should prioritize healing heroic allies over grunt allies.
system.runningMonster:
Acolytes are intended to be a base for generic grunt enemies that focus on being a healer. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Priest’ generic enemy.

Acolytes can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Acolytes can use either a channeling weapon or a light melee weapon + shield. Acolytes can wear anything from no armor, light armor to medium armor. In the stat block, a light melee weapon + shield and light armor is assumed.

system.description: Your Healing spells do not provoke attacks of opportunity.
You heal the target for 11 + (2 x Power)

system.biography:
Alchemic Golems are formidable constructs meticulously crafted by skilled Artificers and Alchemists. These hulking guardians come in various configurations, each tailored to serve specific security purposes within their designated domains. Typically stationed as protectors, Alchemic Golems stand sentinel over valuable treasures, ancient secrets, and critical research facilities, ensuring that only those deemed worthy may pass.

Despite their imposing size and intricate designs, each Golem exhibits a unique blend of alchemical prowess and mechanical ingenuity, reflecting the expertise of their creators. Adventurers delving into forgotten ruins or exploring cutting-edge research facilities can expect to encounter diverse variants of these sentinels. Whether guarding the remnants of a lost civilization or the forefront of arcane experimentation, Alchemic Golems present both a significant challenge and a testament to the enduring legacy of their makers.

details.appearance: x
details.habitat: x

system.tactics:
The Alchemic Golem is a powerhouse able to take on an entire party on its own.  With its high action economy and its ability to mitigate damage every turn it can create a significant challenge for any party.  

You'll want to run the Alchemic Golem in an enclosed space where it can utilize Transmute Low Wall to force players (especially ranged ones) to waste AP on movement.  By using the wall to create a small "pool" you can then flood the pool with Alchemic Flare to prep it for next turn.  Make sure you tell players that are within the pool that they can smell gas to foreshadow the attack.  On the next turn you can use Alchemic Flare to punish any players within the pool, forcing them to abide by your mechanics.

The Alchemic Golem is a beast in close range too.  Move into melee range and deliver all of your AP in light and heavy attacks of your choice and then fire Transmutation Cannon to knock them away.  You can create a more mechanical fight by utilizing enemy positionings and walls to maximize Transmutation Cannon's damage.

Zero Impact Generator should be used anytime damage is taken by the Golem or any of its other body parts.

Alchemic Barrage is a ticking timer, that forces the party to press the attack by whittling down their RP or HP.  Once the Golem is below 50% health it unlocks Alchemic Barrage II, which allows you to focus down a player who is low RP, or force them into taking cover.

Once at half health, Alchemic Golem engages Overdrive which grants it +2 extra AP, further increasing the pressure.

You want to encourage the players to be creative and attack the specific bodyparts to reduce the Golem's action economy.  Make sure you emphasize which body part is doing which attack and that the Zero Impact Generator only protects other bodyparts.  The Golem itself has incredibly high HP, so its worth it for the party to attack those parts.  If they aren't getting the picture, try some forced skill checks to realize what is going on, or even use a NPC companion to attack the bodyparts while showcasing the effectiveness of it.

If the party attacks any body part that doesn't have a special effect, just have the damage translate to the body, but also make sure to let them know it seems to have little effect.  Once one of the bodyparts reaches 0 HP, it is destroyed and its linked actions are no longer available.
system.runningMonster:
Alchemic Golem is a great end of arc boss, providing a high amount of danger.  It can face a party by itself with its high action economy and can be mixed with other creatures to face off against higher level enemies.

The main body of the Golem should be at least 20ft x 20ft.

You'll also want to run this enemy in an enclosed space with a small amount of key line of sight cover.  A space around 120ft x 70ft with walls on all sides is recommended.  If you would like to do a larger space, make sure that you increase the width of Transmute Low Wall to match, but big open fields are not recommended for this enemy.

system.description: This creature gaines +2 extra AP at the start of every turn after its been reduced to less than 50% HP.
This creature has 40 block, but cannot dodge.

Creates a 3ft high wall that counts as difficult terrain.  The wall extends up to 120 feet and lasts for 10 minutes, or until Alchemic Flare or Transmute Low Wall are used, causing the wall to crumble.

Creates an area filled with explosive gas, contained by the wall of Transmute Low Wall (Body).

If an area of gas already exists from a previous turn, ignite the gas into a fireball dealing heavy attack fire damage in the entire area that the gas was in.  Sure Hit.

Fires a transmutation cannon, unleashing a blast of energy that deals light attack damage.  Regardless of if the attack hits or not, the target must make a save against DC 15 or be knocked back 30 feet.  If the target hits a wall or another creature, both creatures take heavy attack damage.
Generates a shield with 35 HP that blocks damage to other body parts except the left arm.
Fires a barrage of missiles, making a light attack with arcane damage against all targets in line of sight.  Has a bonus +10 to accuracy.

Mark a target at the end of this creature's turn if there is no mark.  Activates again at the start of the creature's turn.  Fires a barrage of light attacks equal to the amount of party members at the marked target equal to the amount of party members and then mark another target.  Has a +10 to accuracy.  If the target is no longer a valid target, trigger the effects of Alchemic Barrage (Backpack) instead, and then mark another target.
system.requirement: Can only be used when less than half health or if one body party is destroyed.

system.biography: A big wolf in charge of a pack.

details.appearance: A big wolf, larger than a normal one.
details.habitat: Usually found in a forest.

system.tactics: If not engaged in melee, the alpha wolf will move up to the most vulnerable target it can reach without provoking attacks of opportunity. It will use Leading Bite against the target if it can get wolves in range with it. If an enemy is prone, it will use Go for the throat.
system.runningMonster:
An alpha wolf should be ran with several normal wolves to provide a good challenge for a group of adventurers. An alpha wolf cannot do much by itself and absolutely needs normal wolves around to function as an enemy.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Direhide (alpha wolf pelt)

system.description: For each other Wolf adjacent to the target, a Wolf gets a +2 bonus to accuracy rolls on attacks against that target.

You always act right before other wolves do. Their initiative is placed as 0.1 higher than that of normal wolves. When you are alive at the encounter start phase, wolves act first in the case of a tied initiative.
You make a Light attack against the target. Afterwards, all allied Wolves may move up to their movement speed closer to the target.
You make a Heavy Attack against the target.

system.biography: An almost mindless creature, the Amanita will attack nearby people if it needs to feed. Otherwise, it is docile unless provoked.

details.appearance: A large mushroom with a spotted red cap. Looks similar to the normal mushroom, but with a size that of a regular person. It also has a face on the stalk, along with a pair of arms and legs attached to it.
details.habitat: Found in damp, dark places.

system.tactics: The Amanita mushroom runs up to the closest target it can see and attacks it normally. Upon taking damage, it will use Poison Spore.
system.runningMonster:
A dozen or so Amanita Mushrooms can make a threatening encounter for the average group of adventurers. They become more dangerous when the player’s movement is restricted, either through the size of the room or by the mushrooms surrounding the party.

Gather Parts: 250 Alchemy units

system.description: You take double damage from Fire damage.
You take no damage from Earth damage.

You release poisonous spores in a 5ft radius around you that last until the start of your next turn. Any creature that ends their turn inside the spores takes full pierce Poison damage equal to your Power + 3.

Poison Spores from multiple mushrooms can stack.

system.biography: The process of animal summoning is usually done by Fae, but any mage can learn it if they are in tune with nature.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics:
The summoner spends the first action of its turn casting Summon Beast. After that, it will use Empower Beast if none of the animals are currently empowered. If there is an empowered one, it will use Bestial Command on that creature, assuming the creature is able to attack.

If the summoner is attacked, it will most likely use the animal shield ability to redirect the attack unless the summoner is high on HP/RP and the attack would kill the animal.
system.runningMonster: The summoner can be run together with another heroic ally. If it is the sole heroic enemy, it should start with several grunt type animals already presummoned.

system.description: When a creature you summoned is within 5ft of you, you may change the target of any attack targeting you to that creature instead. Only works if the creature isn’t already targeted as part of the attack.

You summon a Wolf, Boar, Giant Spider or Cheetah (Chosen randomly). This creature is friendly to you and you may direct its actions in combat. It acts at initiative 0. It lasts until the end of the encounter, or until either your or its HP reaches 0 or lower, after which it immediately disappears.
You empower a chosen animal, granting them +2 maximum AP and AP recovery until the end of the encounter.
The target may immediately spend their AP as if they had taken their turn.

system.biography: Apprentices are beginning spellcasters without a specialization. They exist in every race, though human mages are the rarest ones.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics: Apprentices prefer to stay in the back, using Glittershards to block off enemy ranged attackers. After that, they will start to cast Missile Barrage until their mana runs out. If engaged in melee, will disengage and attempt to move away.
system.runningMonster:
Apprentices are intended to be a base for generic grunt enemies that focus on being both a ranged controller and AoE striker. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Mage’ generic enemy.

Apprentices can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Apprentices generally use a channeling weapon and wear no armor.

system.description: When taking the Block action while you have at least 1 mana, your Guard is increased by an additional 8.

Numerous sparkling arcane crystals swarm the area and block line of sight.  Targets inside of or within 5ft of the Glittershards can only see up to 5ft into or out of Glittershards.  Glittershards lasts for up to 10 minutes and you can only have 1 Glittershards active at a time.  You can end this effect for 0 AP on your turn.
You make a Light attack that deals Arcane damage to all enemies within range.

system.biography: Archer is a name given to all users of ranged weaponry, regardless of whether they use a bow or not. They exist in every race and can use a wide variety of ranged weapons.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics: The archer's strategy in combat is to sit still as far away as possible and do damage to the most vulnerable target, usually a spellcaster not in cover. When engaged in melee, they will swap to a melee weapon if they have one.
system.runningMonster:
Archers are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on ranged combat. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Sniper’ generic enemy.

Archers can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Archers can use any type of ranged weapon, though pistols, shotguns and sniper rifles are rarely seen. Archers often wear no or light armor. Most will also carry a light melee weapon as a backup weapon.

system.description: If you didn’t move since the start of your last turn, you gain a +1d4 bonus to all accuracy checks.

system.biography: A type of large spider that has evolved into having a thick armored carapace, giving it more bulk than other spider species.

details.appearance: A large spider covered in a thick carapace.
details.habitat: The armored spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.

system.tactics:
The armored spider will move up and attacks the nearest enemy target, using Poison Bite whenever it can.

If it gets targeted by an attack it will use Defensive Curl, then use Block every time it can while the stance lasts.
system.runningMonster: The armored spider should be run in combination with other types of spiders.

system.description: When using the Block reaction, gain +5 guard (Added into the stats already).
You can walk on walls as if it were solid ground. You ignore webbing and other difficult terrain created by spiders.
When making an opportunity attack, you are treated as having 4 higher Focus and Power.

You folds yourself, entering a defensive stance. While in this stance, you can use the Block reaction for 0 RP. You cannot willingly end the stance and cannot make reaction attacks while on it.

 

The stance lasts until the end of the current creature’s turn.
You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already dazed, it takes 8 full pierce Poison damage instead.

system.biography: While the original assassins come from the desert city of Telsin, the term has evolved since then. It now refers to any sort of stealthy individual who seeks to eliminate priority targets quickly and efficiently. They exist in the employ of all major nations in the world, and people with a similar skill set are not hard to find in adventurer’s guilds, as well as other organizations.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
details.strongAgainst: Parties with low perception, Low defense parties

system.tactics: Assassins aim for the backline, targeting enemy mages or archers. They aim to creep up while stealthed, then go in for a backstab. Once they’re on a target, they will keep attacking that target, using Evasive Maneuver aggressively if needed. If they get swarmed, they will use the disengage action and retreat to wait for a better opportunity to strike again.
system.runningMonster:
Assassins are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on skirmishing. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Rogue’ generic enemy.

An assassin can be run as a threat alongside several grunts, as a small group of 2-3 assassins or in a balanced group of heroic enemies combining it with others of its type like the Defender, Sniper etc.

Assassins prefer light or no armor along with a pair of light weapons, usually daggers.

system.description: You start the battle in stealth (10+Your stealth skill bonus) unless spotted or visible before the battle starts.
You may use the Disengage action for 0 AP.
You make a Heavy attack against the target.
You make a Light attack against the target.
You move 5ft in any direction and do not trigger any Attacks of Opportunity from this movement.

system.biography: A type of large spiders that has suffered from astral corruption, giving it teleportation abilities.

details.appearance: A large spider whose form seems almost transparent.
details.habitat: The astral spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.

system.tactics: The Astral Spider will start hidden and remain hidden until an enemy has moved the range of its blink. When that happens, it will Blink onto that target, choosing the least armored one if multiple targets are available, and attack it. After that, it will use Poison Bite each time it can.
system.runningMonster: The astral spiders should be run with several other of the grunt spiders. Don't run too many at the same time, as an ambush from many blinks at the same time can easily leave a character dead.

system.description: You are permanently hidden until you attack or you are spotted with a perception check like normal (DC23).
You can walk on walls as if it were solid ground. You ignore webbing and other difficult terrain created by spiders.
You teleport to an empty space within range. The next basic Heavy attack you make has it AP cost reduced to 0.
You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already dazed, it takes 8 full pierce Poison damage instead.

system.biography: The astral tiger is a tiger that has been corrupted by Astra. It phases in and out of reality at seeming random times, though the beast itself always seem perfectly aware of how it will move.

details.appearance: A translucent tiger.
details.habitat: Usually found close to the astra line. Rarely found in places that have normal tigers.

system.tactics: An astral tiger’s main strategy is to use Desync to reposition out of range of their melee attackers or to approach ranged attackers. They will prioritize jumping on people with low HP or RP to hit them with their Resync Bite.
system.runningMonster:
Three to four astral tigers is decent challenge for a group of adventurers.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Astra Tiger Pelt

system.description: Your position is constantly in flux, even when not moving. Single target Sure Hit attacks are treated as Lock-on against you. You have 0 guard, but gain +2 dodge (already added to stats).
You teleport up to 20ft.
system.requirement: Can only be used after successfully dodging an attack.

system.description: You make a light attack against a target within range.
system.requirement: Can only be used after teleporting with Desync.

system.biography:
An astra corrupted magpie.

By Mega Mike 70

details.appearance: Two eyes on each side of its head (four total) otherwise looks like a larger magpie.
details.habitat: The astra line.

system.tactics: The astran magpie follows the targeting order described in its Strike of the Shiny ability. It will use Swooping Strike exclusively.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of astran magpies + 1 or 2 greater astran magpie's make a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Due to the tendency to go for shiny armored targets, they can be a lot less scary if the group has a heavy tank and no person wearing valuables.

Gather Parts: 50u of feathersteel from their talons.

system.description: You gain a +1 bonus to your accuracy rolls (max +3) for each other Astran Magpie attacking the same target this round. All Astran Magpie's take their turn at the same time.

You are predisposed to attack targets who are displaying the most valuable items, Crafter numerical bonuses (Focus, Power, Crafting skill) are not perceptible but things like layering for armor or alloying weapons are, You prioritize value on weapons and artifacts, but if none of that is visible then you will default to attacking the one with the shiniest armor.

You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so.

If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.
You may Sidestep up to twice your speed. At any point during this movement, you may make a Light attack.

system.biography: Angry furry cat

details.appearance: A bipedal furry monster with massive Mithril claws.
details.habitat: The heartwood in the astra line

system.tactics:
The bandersnatch starts with Dire Claw at the start of its turn. If it cannot reach any enemies without moving or if it can finish off an injured target, it will use Mana Razor Alpha.

The rest of its abilities are used immediately when they become available.
system.runningMonster:
A single bandersnatch is a challenging encounter for a party.

Gather Parts: 2 claws, each containing 2000 units of mithril. Can be gathered from twice, once for each claw.

system.description:
Your form blurs as it moves, due to distortions it creates in space using its mana aura. You have 25 Evasion while in The Blur. When hit by an attack or when using a defensive action, you lose The Blur. While in The Blur, you are immune to damage that is triggered by evasion/dodge such as the Axe weapon group passive.

You regain The Blur at the start of your turn.
You gain a +1 bonus to saves.

Your eyes flash into an aura sight temporarily and make a Heavy attack against the target. This attack deals double Heavy damage, but the damage is reduced to 1 i the target blocks.

If the target does not react to this attack, it gains Sure Hit.
Your melee attacks gain an additional 60ft range. They are still counted as melee attacks and do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

All enemies must make a save against your potency (10+Focus) or become stricken with irrational fear. While feared, all their attacks targeting you cost +1 AP and you gain +4 to hit against them.

This debuff lasts until they hit you or you dodge or block one of their attacks.
system.requirement: Can only be used the turn after The Blur breaks for the first time.

system.description:
You target an enemy within range and begin to rapidly slash at them. Every time you are attacked by anyone, you may make a light attack against the target of this ability. On damage, you recover 4 HP.

Lasts until you lose The Blur.
system.requirement: Can only be used once. Can only be used after your HP reaches 50%.

system.description: You mark an enemy within range. On the start of your next turn, you may Sidestep towards them in a direct line if possible. If you do, you may immediately make 2 light attacks against the target upon arriving.
system.requirement: Can only be used after Vital Flurry has been used and has been canceled.

system.description: You swipe at the nearest enemy and toss them 30ft away in a direction of your choice. The target passes through allies for this movement, but will collide with walls. If they hit a wall, they take 1d4 true damage and are dazed until the start of your next turn.
system.requirement: Can only be used while your HP is at 25% or lower.

system.biography: A common bear. Not a threat to adventurers, but still dangerous to the average person.

details.appearance: A large bear.
details.habitat: Found in the forest in many places.

system.tactics: The bear attacks the nearest target with Maul and light attacks
system.runningMonster:
A large group of bears is required for them to be a serious threat to a group of adventurers.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides or food units (meat).

system.description: When you deal damage to a target, they become Unbalanced. If they are already Unbalanced, they become Dazed.
You makes a Heavy attack against the target that deals maximum Heavy damage. This attack automatically misses if the target uses the Dodge reaction.

system.biography: To do.

details.appearance: An ominous figure clad in heavy black armor that rides on top of a steed made out of shadows.
details.habitat: Found in the astra line.

system.tactics:
The black knight will use Black Knight's Charge whenever it can target someone more than 20ft away. If it is surrounded by 2 or more enemies, it will use Sweep. It will also use sweep if it allows the use of the charge. After using their Black Knight's Charge, it will always use Impale if it can.

Finally, if it ever gets dismounted it will use its Esoteric Art: All Out. It makes blocking useless, but it can still dodge.
system.runningMonster: A single Black Knight will provide a challenge for an adventuring party. Like all mounted enemies, it will shine in open spaces and struggle in enclosed spaces.

system.description: You are riding on a mount. The mount has a separate 75 HP, uses your defensive stats and follows normal horse mount rules. While mounted, you can only move in a straight line while taking a movement action. After losing your mount, your movement speed is reduced to 20ft. While above 0 HP, your mount heals for your Toughness HP at the start of your turn.
You heal for Toughness x 3 HP at the start of your turn.
You have 10ft reach, but your weapon is otherwise treated as a Light axe.

You may move up to twice your movement in a straight line towards a target further than 20ft away and gain Trample after moving at least 20ft. While under the effects of trample, you don't provoke attacks of opportunity by moving and you can move into enemies that are at least one size smaller than your mount. An enemy may spend 1 RP to move out of the way to an empty spot within 5ft of them.

If they don’t move out of the way, you make a Sure Hit Light attack against them. On damage, you knock them prone into the square you came from and keep moving, occupying the square they were in. Otherwise your movement action ends.

When you reach the target you make a Heavy attack against them. On damage, you may select a different target further than 20ft away, moving towards them and repeating this attack at no additional cost. You may only do this once.
You make a Light attack against all enemies in range. On damage, they are pushed back 10ft.

You make a Heavy attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes rooted until the start of your next turn.

Combo: If used after Black Knight’s Charge, this ability’s cost is reduced to 1 AP and the attack gains Full Pierce.
You discard your armor and shield and focus on offense. You reduce your Guard and Block to 0, but gain an additional 2 AP per turn.

system.biography: A common boar.

details.appearance: A boar.
details.habitat: Can be found in many places in the wild.

system.tactics: The boar will use Goring Charge if possible and there’s no enemy in range. Else it will simply attack or move closer to attack.
system.runningMonster:
Boars need to be a large pack, 10+ to pose a challenge to a group of adventurer’s. A boar can serve as a pet to a heroic unit. Boars are strongest when they fight in an open field where their charge will leave them out of range of counterattacks. In terrain with many obstacles, they may find themselves caught without much to do.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides or food units (meat).

system.description: You gain a +1 bonus to your guard and +2 bonus to Block (already added to stats).

You move up to 4 times your movement speed in a straight line and make a Heavy attack against the target. This attack deals maximum heavy damage if it hits. If it misses, the target moves out of the way and you keep charging until you’ve reached your max movement or until you hit a target or object. All of your movement with this ability does not provoke attacks of opportunity. 

Requires at least 10ft of unimposed movement to start.

system.biography: The broodmother is a giant spider that births other spiders.

details.appearance: A giant spider with a dozen of red eyes.
details.habitat: The broodmother lives in caves or underground, covering the tunnels with webbing.

system.tactics:
The core part of the broodmother's strategy is the Webbing and Feast skills. The broodmother will always cast Webbing on an enemy if there are no enemies it can safely reach and attack currently inside a web. It gains Lock-on against enemies inside the web, even if they aren't rooted, so it will prioritize attacks on those enemies. It will use Poison Bite each time it can.

The feast ability has a 4 AP cost and the setup keyword, meaning that it can't immediately finish even if the broodmother has 4 AP. The smartest way to use Feast is to only use it when the broodmother has 0 AP left, this will let the broodmother get in the maximum number of attacks even if the feast attempt fails due to the target being freed from the web. However, as the GM you can use this variable cost to make the fight easier if needed.
system.runningMonster:
The broodmother is intended as a mostly solo fight, though against stronger groups or groups that have easy access to fire you can add in a few of the grunt spiders.

The burrowing spiders that appear from the broodmother's passive should act on initiative 0. This gives players enough time to deal with them if they play well and they don't risk getting burrowed in without being able to do anything against it.

system.description: You can walk on walls as if it were solid ground. You ignore webbing and other difficult terrain created by spiders.
When you take damage from a weapon attack, a Burrowing Spider appears next to you, closest to the point of impact of the attack.
When attacking a target that is Slowed or Rooted by webs, you gain Lock-On on your basic Light and Heavy Attack.

You prepare to eat a rooted target. When the setup finishes, you make a Heavy attack that deals maximum damage. On damage, you eat the target. The target becomes Stunned inside you. At the start of each of its turns, it takes Heavy full pierce damage until you die.

 

Any attacks made from inside you gains Sure Hit, Full Pierce and deals double damage.
You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already dazed, it takes 8 full pierce Poison damage instead.

You cover a 30x30ft square surface in webs. All creatures in the webbed area become slowed. The webs last until this ability is used again, or until the webs take fire damage on which they are immediately destroyed. Any creature touching the webbing when it is lit on fire becomes Burning 10.

 

Any creature that ends their turn in the webbed area becomes rooted. This lasts until they or an ally spends 4 AP to free themselves. After a unit is freed from the webs, they cannot become rooted by the same web until the end of their next turn. If the webbing is destroyed, a rooted creature is also immediately freed.

system.biography: Brutes are combatants that specialize in melee combat. They exist in every race and civilization and can use a wide variety of weapons and armor.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics: Brute engage the frontline in combat and hit the most vulnerable target there. If they can’t make a Heavy attack, they will use Slam if possible. If they have to get in range first, they will use Charge to do so.
system.runningMonster:
Brutes are intended to be a base for generic Grunt enemies that focus on being a hardhitting melee. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Warrior’ generic enemy.

Brutes can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Brutes generally use heavy melee weapons. They can use no armor, light armor or medium armor depending on the race. The stat block below assumes light armor and a 2handed melee weapon. Some might carry a ranged weapon as backup.

system.description: You may spend 2 or 4 AP on this ability and move as though you had spent that AP on movement. After you finish moving, you may spend half of the AP you used on this ability on light or heavy melee attacks.
You make a Light attack against the target  On damage, the target is moved 5ft away from you if the target is no more than twice your size.

system.biography: A tiny spider that is like a parasite. Once it finds its way inside a host, it eats its way to the targets heart.

details.appearance: A tiny spider.
details.habitat: The burrowing spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.

system.tactics: A burrowing spider will move up to the closest target. If it can, it will use Burrow. Once it is inside a host, it will use Dig Deeper each turn.
system.runningMonster: A burrowing spider is not much of a threat by itself, or even in a large group. A burrowing spider is only dangerous if its ignored, since it takes them a turn of being in melee range before they use burrow and become dangerous. Have them drop down on players or come from behind or from little nooks to allow them to get close. But always give players enough time to react to them.

system.description: When you become the target of an attack, the creature you are burrowed in takes the damage as well, even if you dodge the attack. Any damage you take is reduced by your host’s Guard against the attack. If the host takes damage from an area attack, you are also automatically hit.
You may use Burrow as an opportunity attack for 0 RP.
You can walk on walls as if it were solid ground. You ignore webbing and other difficult terrain created by spiders.
You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, you burrow yourself inside of the target. While burrowed, you shares the same space as the creature you burrowed in and move with it.
You deal maximum Light damage to the target. If you used this ability on your previous turn, it deals double the damage it dealt last time.

system.biography: A spotted big cat.

details.appearance: A large feline with a spotted skin.
details.habitat: Savannah's and temperate to hot deserts.

system.tactics: The cheetah rushes in with its pounce ability then fights as normal.
system.runningMonster:
Cheetahs are only a threat against adventurers when they appear in a group. Putting them a decent distance away from the players so they can use their pounce ability to its maximum effect can help even things out.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides or food units (meat).

system.description: On damage by any attacks made through the Pounce ability, you knock the target Prone.
You may move up to twice your speed towards an enemy and then make 2 AP worth of attacks against them.

system.biography: A large fiend that feeds on the purple crystals that are embedded in its skin.

details.appearance: A large gray fiend with purple crystals embedded into its skin.
details.habitat: The Corwood in the astra line.
details.weakAgainst: The elemental races that absorb damage.

system.tactics:
The crystal behemoth automatically reacts with Crystal Barrier when targeted with an attack if it can.

If it can use Crystal Burst, it will. Otherwise, it will use Crystal Stomp.

If it's close to an enemy, it will use Rock Crunching Bite and a mix of Light and Heavy attacks. If it struggles to reach an enemy, it will instead use Astra Beams spending all its AP on it. If it identifies a silver weapon threat, it will try to focus that enemy.
system.runningMonster:
The crystal behemoth is a suitable threat to a party. It can be defeated in two ways, either by draining its mana to 0 by letting it use crystal burst or by defeating it the normal way. The crystal burst way ensures even parties without magic users can defeat it, though they it will most likely not be a great fight for them.

Note that it will not drop a core if it kills itself with crystal burst.

Drops: Crystal Behemoth Core

system.description: You heal for Toughness x 3 HP at the start of your turn.
You can perfectly detect any creature within 120ft with a spirit core higher than 100.

When you take Arcane, Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Holy or Dark damage or any of its subtypes, you charge your crystals. Your next Crystal Stomp does additional damage equal to the Power of the attacker and the damage type of it changes to the type you took. Does not stack.
You make a Heavy attack against the target. You don’t add your focus to this roll.
You reduce the damage you take by 5 until the start of your next turn..
system.requirement: May not have used Crystal Stomp your last turn.

system.description: You make a Light attack that deals Astra damage to all enemies in range. You also take that amount of true damage and your max HP is lowered by that amount. If this reduces your mana to 0, you explode and deal an additional Sure Hit & Full Pierce heavy damage to all enemies in range, after which you die. When you die in this way, you do not drop a fiend core.
system.requirement: Your absorb magic did not trigger since the end of your last turn.

system.description: You stomp the ground and create a shockwave, making a Light attack against all enemies in range.

You make X separate Light attacks that deal Astra damage against the target. If your Absorb Magic trait is active, you gain the Power bonus for each of these attacks and the element changes to that of the magic absorbed.

details.habitat: Found in damp, dark places.

system.tactics: The deathcap mushroom will start the fight by using Spore Launch at the largest group of enemies it can reach. After that, it will fight normally. When it takes damage, it will use Poison Spore as a reaction.
system.runningMonster:
Two deathcap mushrooms or a deathcap mushroom combined with several amanita mushrooms can provide a suitable threat for a group of adventurers. A deathcap mushroom can provide a lasting debuff to a party that does not have ways to remove poison.

Gather Parts: 500 alchemy units

system.description: You take double damage from Fire damage.
You take no damage from Earth damage.

You release poisonous spores in a 5ft radius around you that last until the start of your next turn. Any creature that ends their turn inside the spores takes full pierce Poison damage equal to your Power + 3.

Poison Spores from multiple mushrooms can stack.

You fire poisonous spores towards an area. All within a 15x15ft area must make a save or take Power full pierce poison damage and become poisoned. The deathcap poison makes the target Sickened while it lasts.

system.biography: Defenders are front liners who go in first and absorb the hits for their allies. Existing in every culture and of any race, they are usually heavily armored with shields.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics: The defender’s combat strategy depends a bit on who their allies are. In general, they want to stick near their vulnerable allies and force melee enemies to attack the defender instead through Threatening Aura. If someone is Challenged, they will use Raise Shield. If they ever hit an attack of opportunity, they will always follow it up with Sweeping Opportunity.
system.runningMonster:
Defenders are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on being a tanky frontline. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Tank’ generic enemy.

Defenders pair best with melee attackers that don’t have as much defense as they do. They can be run with a bunch of Grunt level allies or with a group of around 3 others of a similar type to them like the Assassin or Sniper etc.

The above stat block assumes they are using Medium Armor and a Shield. Any melee weapon can work for a defender, though polearms are the best option.

system.description: If you make an attack of opportunity, you can make a Heavy attack for 0 RP instead of 1. You gain a +2 bonus to accuracy checks when making attacks of opportunity.
Until the start of your next turn, all enemies in your melee range are considered Challenged by you.
Your next Block action against an enemy Challenged by you costs 0 RP.
The target falls prone.
system.requirement: You hit an enemy with an Attack of Opportunity.

system.biography:
Summoning Cost: 1 AP, 1 Mana

10x10ft size

system.description: This summon has an upkeep of 1 AP per creature and counts as 1 towards your summon limit.
You only take 1 damage for each single-target attack but can take full damage from AoE attacks. You cannot make normal attacks.
At the end of your turn, you deal a base 1 true damage + 1 true damage to all enemies for each part of your token that is touching the target.

A creature with Rush gets a turn immediately when being summoned, and the summoning range is increased to 60ft.  If summoned in the middle of your turn, then take this creature's turn first, then finish the remainder of your turn.

You can passively hover up to 5ft above the ground. While hovering, you are not an eligible target for abilities that require a target to be flying or airborne unless you'd meet those conditions normally.
Placeholder ability so site doesn't break

system.biography: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. Though they spent most of their time sleeping in their caves, they are hostile to all living creatures and view them are little more than prey.

details.appearance: A large scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
details.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.

system.tactics:
The drake will begin the fight by flying and attacking the party from the sky. It can use both Fireball and Flame Breath in the same turn while flying. If its mana runs out before being forced to the ground, it will land itself and attack as normal.

If the drake is forced to land through its soft wings ability, it will stay grounded unless it can take flight again without provoking attacks of opportunities. It can still use its Flame Breath even while on the ground, as long as it still has mana.
system.runningMonster:
A group of drakes can provide a good challenge to an adventuring party, though they might be too much to handle depending on the party composition.

Running a pair of drake as a harasser from the sky can make a fight that drains the party's resources without there being a significant risk of anyone dying.

A drake is a size bigger than the wyrmling and a normal humanoid character.

Gather Parts: 250 units of Dragonscale.

system.description: You take only half damage from all fire damage.

You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so.

If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.
You gain +1 Guard, and a further +2 Guard when taking the Block action (Already added to stats).
You breathe fire in a 30ft cone, making a Light attack against all creatures in it. On damage, a target becomes Burning X, where X is your Power x 3.
You make a Light attack against every creature in a 15x15 ft square. On damage, a target becomes Burning X, where X is your Power x 3.

system.biography: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. The wyrmling is a young wyrm that has not yet matured. Despite their age, they are not any less hostile and vicious - attacking any unknown creature that approaches it.

details.appearance: A small scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
details.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.

system.tactics: The wyrmling will stay at range when it can and use its Firebolt ability to weaken the enemy. When engaged in melee, it will fight as normal.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of wyrmlings will provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. They can also be used together with their stronger relatives like the drake and wyrm.

Gather Parts: 100 units of dragonscale.

system.description: You take only half damage from all fire damage.
You can fly while moving, but fall down to the ground after your movement.
You make a Light (1 AP) or Heavy (2 AP) attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes Burning X, where X is your Power x 3.

system.biography: A formless creature that only ever appears in someone's dreams. It can seemingly enter the dream of anyone, no matter how far away they are. Targets people that are alone and enjoys tormenting its prey until they eventually die to exhaustion. Once it has chosen its target, it will keep visiting it until either it or the victim dies.

details.appearance: Varies
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics:
Against a single enemy, the dreameater will do a normal round of combat then do the Nightmare cage on the following round. Immediately following that with Dream Ender on the turn after.

Against a group of enemies, it will do the same thing if it wins initiative. Otherwise, it will immediately cast Nightmare Cage on the target that it was targeting while alone. Once the cage is broken, it has little else going for it and can only do basic attacks.

Should it kill a target with Dream Ender, it will keep repeating the Nightmare Cage into Dream Ender loop until all enemies are defeated.
system.runningMonster:
The dreameater will initially target a single player, preferably one who goes to bed early or who is separate from the rest of the party. They will wake up fighting an enemy they likely cannot defeat by themselves. Any HP or Mana they spent during this is not actually used. Afterwards, they will wake up normally and feel like they had a bad dream.

The dreameater will keep targeting the same player every night if no actions are taken.

The players must go to sleep near each other and at the same time in order to all fight it. Once they do, the dream eater will most likely be an easy kill.

If your party has less than 4 players, be sure to adjust the HP on the cage accordingly.

system.description: The dreameater only attacks sleeping targets and a battle against the dream eater does not take place in the physical world, but in a dreamscape created by it. A creature that is ‘killed’ by the dreameater does not die. Instead, they do not gain the normal benefits of resting and their mana is reduced by 2. If their mana would go below 0 because of this, they instead lose 5 Max HP per mana that could not be reduced. This effect lasts until the creature completes a rest undisturbed by the dreameater or until the dreameater dies.

While in a dreamspace created by a dreameater, all abilities that have restrictions such as “Can only be used once per X.” or “You regain the use of this ability after a rest.” cannot be used. The exception to this is abilities that say “Can only be used once per encounter.” or “You regain the use of this ability at the Encounter Conclusion Phase”.

You change your own form or the dreamscape to something that frightens or surprises the targets. All creatures within range must make a Save or become Shaken.

What a creature targeted by this sees is unique to each creature.

You trap the target in a magical cage and teleport them next to you. The target becomes Stunned.

The cage can be targeted by attacks. Attacks against it cannot miss, it has 55 HP, no reactions and has a base guard of 0. When its HP reaches 0 or if your HP reaches 0, the cage is destroyed.

When the cage is destroyed, the trapped target may immediately take a turn after the current creature’s turn has ended, regardless of their initiative. They do double damage during this turn. Their initiative does not change based on this immediate turn.
You kill the target and regain all your HP.
system.requirement: Target must be trapped by Nightmare Cage

system.biography: A common slime type creature corrupted by Astra. Now hostile to any living creature it sees.

details.appearance: A creature made from a black goo type substance.
details.habitat: Found in astra corrupted area's

system.tactics:
A melee dredge ooze will move to the nearest enemy it can reach and attack them. It will not move if it can still attack a creature.

A ranged dredge ooze will remain stationary unless it can only attack something by moving.
system.runningMonster:
The Dredge ooze is a creature that can snowball out of control if left unchecked. Use a lower amount of them than for a normal grunt fight, around 12 for a 4 man party. If the players have strong anti-grunt tools, you can consider adding more.

You should divide the Dredge Ooze into melee and ranged ones, and only use the ranged attack on those ranged ones. Because of their wall climb nature, you can put them on top of cliffs or hanging from the ceiling.

Gather Parts: Dredge Ooze Sludge worth 700 Clim. It's an alchemy ingredient that can be used to make [REDACTED].

system.description: If you did not move in your last turn, your AP recovery and maximum AP increase by 1 (up to a maximum of 1).

You fire a blast of black sludge at the enemy. You make a Light attack against the enemy, dealing Astra damage on hit.

You may spend 2 AP to make a Heavy or Precise attack instead.

system.biography:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

details.appearance: A small cute slime.

system.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Ghimslag flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Earth Herb.

system.description: You gain 10 Damage Reduction against physical damage, but cannot Block or Dodge attacks.

You take half damage from Earth and Lightning attacks or damage, but you take 50% more from Wind type attacks and damage. You also take half damage from physical attacks, but your movement speed is halved.
Your attacks may deal Earth or Physical damage. When you deal Earth damage, the target must make a Save or becomes Slowed until the end of their next turn.
You gain Damage Reduction 100 against physical damage from the triggering attack
Combine with a compatible target slime, adding HP and MP together. This can't go over the maximum, but if this results in a slime with maximum health, it restores 1 RP too.
system.requirement: Target must also have the Combine ability.

system.description: You make a light attack against the target. On hit, the target becomes rooted until they spend 1 AP, which removes all slimes that used this action. If the target took damage from this, the AP cost is increased to 2.

system.tactics: The Efreet seeks to move up alongside their Unstable Efreet.
system.runningMonster: Best paired with several Unstable Efreet.

system.description: When your HP is lowered to 0, you will immediately use Explode Self as a reaction. After that, you immediately die.
You take half damage from all fire damage and your attacks deal fire damage.

When you reach 0 HP, you will begin to explode. This explosion happens at the start of the turn of the character who triggered this effect. When it does, the Efreet may make a Heavy attack against all creatures within range.
All creatures within range must make a save or take Light Fire damage.

system.biography: Legends say these wolves were once normal forest predators who stumbled upon a fey nexus or were subject to an otherworldly curse. Over generations, they’ve adapted, developing unique teleportation powers fueled by a blend of spiritual mana and wild fae energy.

details.appearance: Faewolves are lean, lupine beasts whose fur shimmers like astral mist. Their eyes burn with a fae-like glow, a sign of their internal magical reserves.
details.habitat: They favor dense forests or snowy highlands close to fey rifts, where ambient magic saturates the environment. Lone Faewolves may venture farther if drawn by potent magical signatures—like adventurers bearing artifacts or high spirit cores.

system.tactics:
The faewolf will start the battle in Shimmer. If it can, it will teleport to the squishiest looking enemy and attack it with a Heavy attack and Arcane Fang.

Every turn while it has mana, it will repeat those moves and use the remaining AP on movement or light attacks.
system.runningMonster:
A group of ~4 faewolves will provide a challenge to a party of 4.

Because of their nature as ambushers and their high mobility, be careful of how you run these. Three wolves teleporting in on anyone may very well down them. Likewise, three arcane fangs on the same target can add a lot of damage quickly. If running a high number of faewolves, skipping the stealth part may be best.

The wolves should all focus fire a target if you want to play them to be deadly, but otherwise you can also have them attack different targets.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Faewolf pelt

system.description: Your form appears half-real in dim or moonlit settings. You begin an encounter hidden unless spotted with a Perception check (e.g., DC 23). If forced into bright light, or if you makes noise (like a howl), the GM can allow another Perception roll to detect it.
You treat natural uneven terrain (rocks, fallen logs, etc.) as normal ground and can leap short spans (5–10ft) without costing extra movement.
You teleport in a brief glow of eerie light to any unoccupied spot within 40 ft. Your next Heavy attack this turn costs 0 AP.

Your bite channels internal magic. You make a Light Attack that deals Arcane damage. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already Dazed, this attack instead deals an additional 8 full pierce Arcane damage as the lingering magic intensifies.

system.biography:
Just a fire slime.

By Nya.

details.appearance: A small cute slime.

system.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Salachar flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Fire Herb.

system.description: You gain 10 Damage Reduction against physical damage, but cannot Block or Dodge attacks.
You take half damage from Fire and Frost attacks or damage, but you take 50% more from Water type attacks and damage. You are immune to Burning.

Your attacks may deal Fire or Physical damage. When you deal Fire damage, you also inflict Burning 2*X where X is your Power. Furthermore, any target ending its turn while rooted by your Consume takes light Fire damage.
You gain Damage Reduction 100 against physical damage from the triggering attack
Combine with a compatible target slime, adding HP and MP together. This can't go over the maximum, but if this results in a slime with maximum health, it restores 1 RP too.
system.requirement: Target must also have the Combine ability.

system.description: You make a light attack against the target. On hit, the target becomes rooted until they spend 1 AP, which removes all slimes that used this action. If the target took damage from this, the AP cost is increased to 2.

system.biography: Summon cost: 4 AP, 4 Mana

system.description: This creature has an upkeep of 2 AP and counts as 2 towards your summon limit.
When an ally within 60ft rolls a 1, they may automatically reroll that roll and accept the new result.
The target must reroll their roll. Can not be used on a roll that was already rerolled.
You shoot a golden coin at an enemy, making a Light attack against the target that deals 2d10 Astra damage, but doesn’t receive bonuses from power.

You may Sidestep 5ft and the attack against you automatically misses.

Roll a d20. If you roll 11 or higher, you recover 2 RP.
system.requirement: You are the target of an attack.

system.biography: An ice elemental type creature that is inherently attracted to the warmth of other creatures. Said to be a manifestation of travelers that got lost in a blizzard and closely related to the yuki-onna youkai. Not a creature with malicious intent necessarily, but her way of thinking may be too alien to negotiate with.

details.appearance: A beautiful woman with pale or blue skin and white hair.
details.habitat: Can be found in any place where it freezes for most of the year.

system.tactics:
The Frost Maiden is an assassin that functions by limiting the enemies vision and luring them apart from each other, then striking an isolated target. 

She will start the battle by using Blizzard. On her first turn, she will use Blizzard Walker and wait around 40ft away from the enemies. If the enemies spread out to look for her, she can move in with Snow Assassin on her next turn to attack a target, then follow it up with normal attacks after.

From that point, she can alternate Blizzard Walker and Snow Assassin to get favorable engagements with a lower amount of enemies present.
system.runningMonster:
A group of frost maiden provides a challenging fight for high spirit core players.

As the GM, you can wait for a turn to see if the players will spread out and stumble into the blizzard alone to look for the frost maiden after the first turn. If they don't, then the frost maiden should just attack to not waste anybody's time. Make sure to hide the token after she moves out of vision range to further tempt people to spread out. Also, remember that if the frost maiden doesn't attack on her first turn, she can use her remaining AP to move and circle around the party to further throw them off about where she is.

system.description: You take no damage from Frost damage.
You may hide inside a blizzard without requiring cover to hide behind.
Your body is freezing cold. Any melee attacks made by you deal Frost damage. Any creature touching you for an extended period of time takes Heavy Frost damage at the start of their turn.

You create a blizzard in a 160ft radius centered on top of you. Any creature in the blizzard that is not immune to frost damage becomes slowed and has their vision reduced to 15ft.

 

Having a suitable heat source nearby or otherwise being protected from the cold removes the slowed effect given by this ability.
You Sidestep up to double your speed. Afterwards, you may stealth for 0 AP. Cannot be used in the same turn as Snow Assassin.

The frost maiden may Sidestep up to double her speed. Afterwards, she may make a Heavy attack against a target. If she was hidden from the target before moving, the target cannot react to the attack.

 

Cannot be used in the same turn as Blizzard Walker.

system.biography: Gargoyles are usually tied to an abandoned place made out of stone where they will lie dormant in their stone form until people approach. When living creatures get close enough, they will reveal themselves and attack them. The reason behind their hostility remains unclear, and most adventurers that don’t want to deal with them simply avoid their resting place.

details.appearance: Gargoyles are medium sized creatures that at a first glance look like statues. Their skin is made of stone and they have a pair of small wings on their back.
details.habitat: Found in abandoned places made out of stone.

system.tactics: Gargoyles will start the fight by flying over the largest group of enemies and using Stone Form. After that, they will fight normally with light and heavy attacks unless they can use Stone Form again without provoking an attack of opportunity. They may use Stone Form even when on the ground if they are isolated and about to take many hits, especially if already low on RP.
system.runningMonster: A small group of gargoyles of around 3-4 will provide a good threat against an average party. Gargoyles should start from a higher point, like at the top of a church or something to let them engage with Stone Form on their terms. Half Pierce attacks completely counter Stone Form, as they ignore the extra guard it gives and the gargoyle can’t react to the attacks at all while in it.

system.description: You gain +2 guard, but lose 2 agility. (Already added to stats)
You may fly during your movement at your normal speed, but if you are still airborne at the end of your turn, you fall to the ground taking fall damage as normal.

You turn yourself to hardened stone, gaining a +10 guard bonus but becoming unable to take any actions. All attacks made against you automatically hit, but cannot crit. You may cancel this effect at the start of your turn.

If used while flying, you drop down to the ground without taking falling damage. Any creature within 5ft of where you land may spend 1 RP or else they take Heavy damage.

system.biography: The ghost is an undead monster that spawned from a person that died while bearing a strong grudge. They are hostile to any living creature around them, mistaking them for the subject of their vengeance.

details.appearance: The ghost's appearance mimics that of the person that died, except more transparent.
details.habitat: Can be found in any place where a person died.

system.tactics:
The ghost will start by throwing objects at its enemies. Once it is engaged in combat, it will use Spectral Touch instead of heavy attacks when attacking an armored enemy.

Against a physical attack, it can always react for free thanks to its Incorporeal ability.
system.runningMonster: Ghost can be a pushover or almost impossible to fight depending on what the party has available. They are intended to operate in groups, but characters that rely purely on physical attacks will struggle to hit it, where as parties with casters or tools such as Sacrament will cut through the ghost without much issues.

system.description: You do not spend your RP when reacting against a physical attack made with a non-magical weapon. A weapon that is enchanted counts as magical.
You may move through solid objects and enemies with no penalty.

You throw an unattended object within range at a target within range, making either a Light (1 AP) or Heavy (2 AP) attack that deals normal listed damage. You do not need to physically interact with the object to throw it.
You attempt to attack the soul of the target with a touch, making a Heavy attack against the target.

system.biography: Ghouls are undead that are perpetually hungry. They feed on the corpses of dead creatures, preferably humanoids.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature with grey skin, sharp teeth and red eyes.
details.habitat: Usually found in places with lots of dead bodies.

system.tactics:
If a ghoul can eat a corpse with Devour Corpse, it will always do so. It may even move to the corpse to do it if it can do so safely.

When in combat, it will use its Ghoul Bite if it can and it is missing HP. Otherwise, it will attack normally.
system.runningMonster: A large group of ghouls can make a good challenge for a group of adventurers. Ghouls become a lot more powerful if they fight in a room or place that has a lot of corpses ready to be devoured. Ghouls can also use Devour Corpse on the bodies of other ghouls.

system.description: Holy damage dealt to you is treated as Full Pierce damage.
If there's a corpse within 5ft of you at the start of your turn, you heal for half your maximum HP and gain a +4 bonus to accuracy checks.
You attempt to bite a target creature making a Heavy attack against them. You heal for the damage this attack deals.
You eat a nearby corpse, instantly devouring it and removing it from the field. You gain +2 AP and your maximum AP is increased by 2 until the end of the encounter.

system.biography:
The ultimate lifeform.

By Nya.

details.appearance: A giant crab
details.habitat: Beaches in the astra line

system.tactics: It's very adaptive, e.g. it will try to counter its opponent's actions. However, it doesn't plan ahead, it simply reacts. It just wants food, and will try to escape death. Peaceful resolution may be possible with sufficiently large offerings?
system.runningMonster:
One giant crab is a good challenge for a group of 4 SC3000+ characters.

Gather Parts: DC25 to harvest a Perfect Shell.

system.description: You have +1 guard and +4 Block, but -2 Evasion (already added to stats). You also have 5 DR against slashing attacks.
Your movement in a straight line gains +10 movement speed.
You may shift up to 2 stat points (except Toughness). The minimum is 3 and maximum is 9.
You Block or Dodge an attack. Then, you automatically Dodge or Block (whichever you didn't before) against the next attack.
You Block a ranged attack, as long as the accuracy roll is below your Dodge value.
You remove all stacks of one status effect from yourself.

You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes rooted until it takes at least 10 damage in one attack. Medium and smaller creatures are forced to move with the crab, but large creatures grabbed by this prevent you from moving more than 5ft away.

Cannot be used against a target already grabbed.

You may let go of a target for 0 AP. You suffer the root penalty for dodging against the target (but only against the target).
The target must make a Save or take Heavy damage.

system.biography: A mantis the size of a regular person. Nobody knows how they grew so big.

details.appearance: A giant mantis
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics:
At the start of the battle, it will leaping strike to the most vulnerable looking target it can safely reach. It will not provoke attacks of opportunity to do so.

Once it’s engaged in combat, it will keep attacking the most vulnerable looking target. It will use slice and dice whenever it can.
system.runningMonster:
The Giant Mantis can cut through unarmored targets extremely quickly if it gets a surprise round. If the party does not have high perception values, then it may be best to not run more than 2 at the same time. If running more than 2, it may be better to forego the stealth part.

Note that the Giant Mantis poses very little threat to an armored target, but it's danger level rises if the party has no armored people.

system.description: You are camouflaged as you stalks your prey. You gain a bonus +10 to stealth checks and can move at full speed while hiding. When you get a surprise round, your initiative is treated as if you had rolled the maximum possible.
You bladelike arms are razor sharp, causing the target to bleed when hit. When you deal damage to a target wearing no armor or light armor, you deals an additional Power true damage.
You jump to a target within range and make a Light attack against it.
You may make two Light attacks against the target.
system.requirement: You must have dealt damage to the target this turn.

system.biography: A fiend that appears like a giant slime. Seeks to devour the mana of other creatures.

details.appearance: A large slime in the colors of the rainbow.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere with astra influence.

system.tactics: If the slime is out of range to attack, it will use Bowling Roller. If it is in range to use Gluttony, it will do so. It will use Digestion when it can on the turn after it hits with Gluttony.
system.runningMonster: A solo monster against which regular attacks will do little. A group with heavy magic damage may be able to kill it normally, but dealing damage without landing a critical hit is nearly impossible. Make sure to give the players enough hints and guidance so that they can realize this.

system.description: Critical attacks deal 125 bonus true damage to you.
You cannot use basic defensive actions: Block or Dodge, but you have 100 Damage Reduction to all non-magical attacks.
You can use Gluttony as an attack of opportunity for 1 RP.
When struck by a magical attack, you gain 100 Damage Reduction to that attack element indefinitely. You can only have one instance of this adaptability at a time.

You begin to quickly roll towards a target with little control.  You move in a straight line towards the target, immediately stopping at the first target or large object in your path and making a Heavy attack against that target.
You attempt to digest all targets affected by Gluttony. Dealing 20 (type) damage with sure hit and full pierce.

You attempt to consume a target, making a Heavy Attack against the target.  On hit, the target is affected by Gluttony and becomes engulfed in slime.  An engulfed target becomes Weakened.  An ally can attempt to pull a consumed target from the slime with a DC20 Power Check, removing the effects of Gluttony.

system.biography: A large spider that preys on regular people.

details.appearance: A large spider.
details.habitat: The giant spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.

system.tactics: The Giant Spider will attempt to Web Spray the closest target if it is not in melee range. Afterwards, it will move up and attack using poison bite whenever it can.
system.runningMonster: A large group of giant spiders can provide a decent challenge to a group of adventurers. Should be combined with other grunt spiders to create a more varied encounter.

system.description: You can walk on walls as if it were solid ground. You ignore webbing and other difficult terrain created by spiders.
You make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already dazed, it takes 8 full pierce Poison damage instead.

You make a Light attack against the target that deals no damage, but covers the target in webs. On hit, the target becomes rooted.This effect lasts until the target or an ally spends 4 AP to remove the webbing.

 

If a creature rooted by this ability takes fire damage, the effect also disappears as the webs burn away.

system.biography: An Exousiai with gravity powers.

details.appearance: A floating ball of meat with 3 metal rings around it.
details.habitat: The corwood in the astra line

system.tactics:
The gravity fiend starts the combat by using Exousiai's Presence. On each of its turns it will use Weight of the World, followed by Gravity Crash if possible.

After that, it will use Gravity Pull to get enemies in range then use Crushing Presence if it can hit enough enemies.

It has high regeneration and is intelligent. If it is threatened, it can attempt to create distance to give it a turn to heal.
system.runningMonster:
The Gravity Fiend is not something you should use against a party and expect them to beat it without preparation. Against an unprepared party of people that are most likely running max burden, it can easily inflict heavy damage or kill people without much counterplay. Due to this, it is rated as danger level EX.

It functions as a solo monster against a whole party of 5 even when they do prepare. Against an average prepared party, this can be considered to be a D rated threat.

system.description: You heal for Toughness x 20 at the start of your turn.
You are immune to any status effects that would cause you to lose AP or otherwise prevent you from acting.
All enemies within 40ft of you are slowed. This applies immediately when they enter this range and lasts for the entire movement of leaving this range.
Any attack against you from further than 40ft away automatically misses.

You can passively hover up to 5ft above the ground. While hovering, you are not an eligible target for abilities that require a target to be flying or airborne unless you'd meet those conditions normally.

You raise the astra level in the zone by 1. All enemies within range that do not have enough resistance to negate this immediately suffer negative effects.

Any creatures suffering from Astra Poisoning immediately have their Astra Poisoning worsened by 1 stage.

Every enemy in range suffers +1 Burden until the end of the encounter. This can stack.

You immediately kill all grunts and summons.
You make a Heavy attack against all enemies within range.
You pull every enemy within range up to 40ft.

You make a Light attack against all enemies within range. 

Against an enemy that's overburdened, this also gains Full Pierce.

system.biography:
An astra corrupted magpie

By Mega Mike 70

details.appearance: Two eyes on each side of its head (four total) otherwise looks like a larger magpie.
details.habitat: The astra line.

system.tactics: A greater astran magpie follows the targeting described in its Strike for the Shiny, smartly! ability. They use Swooping Strike II almost exclusively, unless they can attack without moving already.
system.runningMonster:
1 or 2 Greater Astran Magpie along with a large group of normal Astran Magpie's makes a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. While a greater astran magpie can be harder to hit than other enemies, keep in mind its damage out is comparatively lower than other heroic enemies.

Gather Parts: 250u of feathersteel from their talons, 250u of direhide from the pelt.

system.description: You gain a +1 bonus to your accuracy rolls (max +6) for each other Astran Magpie attacking the same target this round.

You are predisposed to attack targets who are displaying the most valuable items, Crafter numerical bonuses (Focus, Power, Crafting skill) are not perceptible but things like layering for armor or alloying weapons are, You prioritize value on weapons and artifacts, but if none of that is visible then you will default to attacking the one with the shiniest armor. You also consider current health, attempting to down (not finish off, just down) low health >25% HP targets as top priority, it’s easier to loot people who can’t fight back after all!

You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so.

If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.
You do not lose altitude for being hit while flying. However, you count as mounted for anti-mount abilities such as Brace.
You may Sidestep up to twice your speed. At any point during this movement, you may make a Heavy attack.

system.biography: The greater manticore is a monstrous combination of three different types of animal originally fused together through magic. They possess little intelligence and do little more than feast on anyone unfortunate enough to run into one. Their second head is a mutation caused by astra corruption that only makes it more vicious.

details.appearance: A large creature with the body of a lion, a scorpion like tail and a large pair of wings.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the wild or in a dungeon.

system.tactics:
The greater manticore has 2 separate attack phases.

The first attack phase should be using the head to attack, starting with Lion's Roar and then attacking slowed targets to gain the bonuses from the crushing maw ability.

The second attack phase should use the tail, using Tail Spikes and then attacking targets that were hit by it if possible.
system.runningMonster:
The greater manticore is a solo monster that has a lot more AP than a normal creature would have thanks to its dual headed ability. You don't need to stick to the head and tail attack phases, but it will make it easier to run and for players to understand.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of primehide.

system.description: When making a basic Light or Heavy attack with your maw, you become enhanced against Slowed targets. If it’s a Light attack, you gain Sure Hit. If it’s a Heavy attack, you gain Full Pierce.
You take two turns. Regardless of initiative, your first turn always comes first in a round. Your second turn comes after half of your enemies have taken their turn.
When making a basic Light or Heavy Attack, you may attack with either your head or tail. You gain a benefit based on the body part chosen.
When making a basic Light or Heavy attack with your tail, you inflict Daze on dealing damage. If the target is already Dazed, you instead deal 5 (Light) or 10 (Heavy) Full Pierce Poison damage.
You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your speed is doubled while doing so.
All enemies within range must make a Save or become Unbalanced. They also become Slowed until the end of your next turn.

You firee a hail of spikes at a 15x15 ft area, making a Light attack against all enemies within the area. On damage, the target becomes Dazed. If the target is already Dazed, they instead take 5 poison damage.

system.biography: The gryphon despite its appearance is an animal that naturally appears in the wild. They are territorial, but not hostile to people that stay far enough away from them.

details.appearance: The gryphon is a large creature has the body of a lion with the wings and head of an eagle.
details.habitat: Found in the mountains or other places with high elevation.

system.tactics:
The gryphon will stay in the sky and harrass with Wind Blast until its mana runs out. If it lands a hit and knocks a target prone, it will follow up with Dive Attack on the target.

If the enemy has a lot of ranged attackers or if they are too spread out for a Wind Blast, the gryphon might go in earlier with a Dive Attack and use regular attacks instead.
system.runningMonster:
A group of gryphons can challenge a group of seasoned adventurers.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Direhide.

system.description:
You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so.

If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.

You move up to 40ft towards a target within range and then make a Light attack against it. On damage, you do not provoke attacks of opportunity for the rest of your turn and may move up to your movement speed at the end of your turn without spending AP.

 

If this attack fails to do damage,you lose your Flight ability and become Grounded until the start of its next turn.
