You fire a large gust of wind at a 30x30 feet square within range. You make a Heavy attack that deals Wind damage against all targets within the area. On damage, the target is blown away to the nearest edge of the square and knocked Prone.

system.biography: The Heliamphora is a large pitcher plant, of which smaller versions are sometimes kept as house plants. It is effectively mindless, just luring in creatures with its pollen and attacking them to eat.

details.appearance: It appears like a giant pitcher plant.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere in a forest or similar area.

system.tactics:
The opening for a Heliamphora is to wait for a target to walk in range of its vines without noticing the plant. It may use Luring Pollen to do so.

After its surprise attack, it will try to put any grabbed creatures in its pitcher whenever possible. If any creatures are more than 10ft away from it, it will use its pollen to lure them closer. After that, it will try to grab as many creatures as possible using its basic attack and vine grab.
system.runningMonster:
Make sure the players are aware of the threat of the pitcher once a player has been grabbed by describing the creature as attempting to move the player to its pitcher. Being dropped in it takes a player out of the fight and may get them killed.

Some players may also need help in recognizing that they can destroy the vines. If you want to go easy on the players, you can delay the first drop in pot and drop hints that the vines can be targeted.

system.description: You are hidden with a Stealth of 30 while pretending to be an ordinary plant until you attack. Luring Pollen does not break camouflage and will not trigger combat when used while creatures are unaware of you.
Fire damage dealt to you is treated as Full Pierce damage.
You have 0 movement and can only be forcefully moved through Secret Art or Climax Art abilities.
You have a melee attack range of 10ft.
Drop a creature rooted by your vine grab in your pitcher. The creature becomes stunned and takes Heavy full piercing damage at the start of its turn until you die.
system.requirement: Can only be used as the first action in a turn, must have a grabbed creature.

system.description: Any creature within range that’s more than 10ft away from the you must make a save. If they fail, they must spend AP on their next turn to move as close to you as possible. Once they are within 5ft of you, the effect ends.

Your vine wraps around the target, rooting it. The vine can be destroyed by attacking it. It has 14 HP and takes double damage from fire damage and Slashing attacks. It cannot make reactions, has 0 guard and attacks against it always hit.

 

A creature can be grabbed by multiple vines at the same time.
system.requirement: Can only be used after dealing damage with a melee attack.

system.biography: Hobgoblins on a boar.

details.appearance: A hobgoblin riding a boar
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics: The boar rider will charge towards the enemy backline, aiming to trample as many enemies on the way there as possible.
system.runningMonster: A large group of boar riders will make a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. As they are a mounted enemy, boar riders excel in open fields and are worse indoors. They can also be combined with other Hobgoblin enemies for a more varied challenge.

system.description: You are riding on a boar mount. The boar mount has a separate 10 HP and follows normal boar mount rules. While mounted, you can only move in a straight line while taking a movement action. After losing your mount, your movement speed is reduced to 20ft.
When under the Trample effect, you can trample enemies the same size as you (Medium). You also deal an additional Power damage with the attack.

You may move up to three times your movement in a straight line and gain Trample for this movement. While under the effects of trample, you don't provoke attacks of opportunity by moving and can move into enemies that are at least one size smaller than your mount. An enemy may spend 1 RP to move out of the way to an empty spot within 5ft of them.

If they don’t move out of the way, you make a Sure Hit Light attack against the,. On damage, you knock them prone into the square you came from and keep moving, occupying the square they were in. Otherwise your movement action ends.

Cannot be used when an enemy unit is visible within 10 feet of you.

system.biography: Gobo

details.appearance: A feral goblin.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics:
A hobgoblin fighter hits the closest target it can reach. If there are multiple, it will hit the one with the least armor. If it cannot reach any target, it will throw a rock.

When a hobgoblin goes below half HP, it will use Gobbo Regeneration.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of Hobgoblins enemies will provide a decent challenge to a group of adventurers starting out. 

It can only use its heal once due to the mana cost. You can also give some of them ranged weapons to create a more balanced enemy group.

system.description: You gain +1 Guard.
You heal yourself for 15+Toughness HP
You deal 2 true damage to the target.

system.biography: A gobo tactician

details.appearance: A feral goblin.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics:
The hobgoblin tactician uses its Stratagem: Lightning at the start of the encounter. When it loses more than 15 HP, it will use its Gobbo Regeneration.

The hobgoblin tactician is smarter than other hobgoblins and can move tactically to hit weaker enemies. It may also choose to take some damage early and save RP to be able to heal the damage up with its self healing.
system.runningMonster: The hobgoblin tactician is best matched with several hobgoblin fighters The tactician can speed up the fighters and get them in range. It uses a 2handed weapon for extra damage.

system.description: Your guard is increased by 2.
You heal yourself for 15+Toughness HP
All allied units (including yourself) gain +1 to initiative and may immediately move up to their speed.
system.range: All allies in sight, including yourself.

system.biography: A weird animal that has three heads that each have their own thoughts. Each head itself is an intelligent creature (though they lack the ability to speak a common language), but the heads themselves are always in conflict. They struggle to make a decision on even the most basic things, sometimes resorting to infighting. Only when their existence is threatened by an outside source do the heads work together.

details.appearance: The hydra is a creature with three heads resting on a long neck attached to a rather small frame. It is usually found with its body below the water with only the three heads sticking out. The necks and heads are covered in colored scales with each of the heads having a different color that marks their element. The Earth one is green, the Frost one is white and the Lightning one is golden.
details.habitat: Almost always found near water. Due to the size of the hydra, usually a large river or lake.

system.tactics: The hydra will open with their Hydra Breath attacks if the enemy isn’t in range, or if they can hit 3+ people with it. Otherwise, they will attempt a constrict into Three Headed Assault on a target when possible.
system.runningMonster:
The Hydra can serve as a solo monster for a party of 4. The regenerative nature of the heads can make it feel to the players that they are not making progress or doing the wrong thing, so make sure to emphasize that the hydra is being slowed and weakened when the heads grow.

The Hydra lacks a strong central body for the players to target, so you can just put 3-5 head tokens to represent the heads (it dies after getting 6+ heads). The heads shouldn’t move more than 5ft away from each other.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of Primehide

system.description: You have 3 heads, each with their own HP and element. Each head has 2 AP, 3 RP and they all use the same stats as listed in the stats block. Roll separate initiative for each head. An AoE attack only does damage to one of the heads, chosen by the attacker.

When a head is killed, two new heads immediately sprout from the defeated heads. These new heads share the element of the original defeated heads and function as two fresh heads as described in the multi-headed ability.
Each head that grows extra past the original 3 lowers your agility by 1 and movement speed by 5ft. When your agility reaches 0 because of this, you die.

Each head has an element. There is an Earth, a Frost, and a Lightning element head. Each head takes half damage from attacks dealing the same type of damage as their element. Their element also influences their Hydra Breath attack.

You breathe in a 30ft cone, making a Light attack against all targets in it. The damage type is based on the head’s element. On damage, you apply an effect based on the head’s element. The Earth head inflicts Daze for 1 turn, the Frost head inflicts Slowed for 1 turn and the Lightning head inflicts Static X for 1 turn, where X is your Power x 3.
You and the target both become rooted. The target may spend 2 AP to break free, after which the target and you are both no longer rooted.
You and all other heads make a Light attack against the target. All heads, except for you, that made an attack regain 1 less AP on their turn.

system.biography:
An ice elemental with high intelligence that commands other elementals and beasts in the area. She does this without directly communicating with them, merely her presence in the area is enough for ice creatures to submit.

She is domineering, but can be reasoned and negotiated with if shown the proper respect.

details.appearance: A beautiful woman with pale or blue skin and white hair. Stands out from the average yuki-onna or frost maiden with her regal stature and the crown of ice she wears on her head.
details.habitat: Can be found in any place where it freezes for most of the year.

system.tactics:
The ice queen will start by summoning a tower near her enemies with both her encounter start action and her normal ability, then immediately follow it up with Reverbant Frost.

She wants to keep away from melee enemies as much as possible. If she can escape them without provoking, she will do so. Future towers will be placed to either slow melee enemies on top of her, or in the biggest group of enemies. She will always follow up a tower placement with Reverbant Frost.

If she has the option to hit slowed enemies safely with Shards of Ice, she will do so. Otherwise she will attack with whatever weapon is most suitable for the situation. She can easily use a ranged weapon to safely attack more vulnerable opponents.
system.runningMonster:
The ice queen is a solo monster that is both intelligent and cunning. She may avoid direct fights if they don't appear to be in her favor or attempt to negotiate if things look dire.

Most of her threat comes from the towers. If players are dedicated to instantly destroying them, she may need reinforcements to keep up the threat.

system.description: You may create any weapon and use it immediately. You are considered proficient in any weapon created through this ability. These weapons may deal Frost damage instead of their normal damage. You may also create two weapons at the same time, but they must be two Light weapons of the same type. You may dismiss these weapons at any time for no cost.
You provoke no attacks of opportunity from Slowed enemies. You gain a +4 bonus to Guard when taking the Block reaction. (Already added to stats)
You take no damage from Frost damage.
Your initiative increases by 5. You may summon 1 tower described in ‘Frost Creation: Tower’ anywhere within range.

You summon a 10ft high frosty tower within range. The tower has 45 HP, 4 guard and no reactions. Attacks against the tower always hit.

The tower acts at initiative 0, at the end of a round. When it does, it makes a single light attack using the your stats at every enemy within 20ft of it. This attack has half pierce, deals Frost damage and on damage, the enemy is Slowed until the end of their next turn.
You fire a shard of ice at every enemy within range, making a Light attack against them that deals Frost damage. This attack gains full-pierce against any enemy that is slowed.
All frost towers created by ‘Frost Creation: Tower’ within range immediately take action, making their single attack listed in the ability.

system.biography: A fiend found in storybook dungeons.

details.appearance: A humanoid shape of ink.
details.habitat: Storybooks.

system.tactics:
The Inkblight moves forward hitting the target that looks the weakest. If targeted by an attack they can dodge, they will use their Inky Dodge to do so.

If they are in a position to use their Ink Attack, they will do so and use the strongest attack possible.
system.runningMonster:
A group of 16 inkblights are a suitable threat for an experienced group of 4 adventurers. Inkblights, like most fiends, are intelligent. They will target squishy looking targets and use their inky dodge to pressure ranged attackers with the teleport.

Recommended spirit core level: 2000-2500.

system.description: When you die, you explode in a blob of ink. You Blind all enemies and create difficult terrain in a 5ft radius around you.
You heal for Toughness HP at the start of your turn.
You take the Dodge action against the triggering attack, then teleport up to 40ft.
system.requirement: You are the target of an attack.

system.description: You make a Light (1 AP) or Heavy (2 AP) attack against the target.
system.requirement: You and the target must both be standing on Ink.

system.biography:
Summoning Cost: 4 AP, 2 Mana

10x10ft size

system.description: This creature has an upkeep of 2 AP and counts as 2 towards your summon limit.
You have +2 guard and +6 Block (already added to stats).

You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so.

If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.

You summon a swarm of insects in a 15x15 square. Any creature except for you, a devouring swarm or a summoner contracted to you ending their turn inside of it takes Full Pierce Light damage.

You may have up to two of these swarms active at the same time.

You move one of your Swarms up to 20ft or you may Sidestep an ally up to 20ft.

You may also spend 1 RP to use this ability instead.
You make a Light attack against the target that deals Physical(Piercing) damage.

You shape the area around you to be like that of your hive. The area within 20ft of you gains the following properties:

  • You gain Tremorsense in your hive area, becoming aware of the exact location of all creatures touching the ground.
  • Any non-flying creature except for you, a devouring swarm or a summoner contracted to you is slowed in the area. 
  • When an enemy dies while in the domain, you may choose to spawn an Ixith swarm in that location without paying the normal cost as a swarm bursts from the corpse. These do not count against your normal limits. In addition, when an enemy dies in your domain you heal for your Toughness x2

Upkeep: 1 Mana. When you pay upkeep, you may increase the radius of your hive by 10ft.

system.biography: 2 AP, 2 Mana to summon

system.description: This summon has an upkeep of 1 AP per creature and counts as 1 towards your summon limit.
You land a critical hit when you roll 18 or higher.
You make a Heavy attack against the target. If the attack hits, it is automatically a critical hit.

system.biography: The landshark is a small beast that travels below the ground and attacks travelers.

details.appearance: A small creature with a large fin.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the wild. Most common in open fields.
details.weakAgainst: Sure hit attacks, other Burrowed creatures

system.tactics:
Landsharks are extremely hard to hit while they are not attacking. They become vulnerable when they leap out to bite, allowing for readied attacks or other reaction attacks to hit them easily. 

Because ranged attackers cannot easily do this, they become the easiest target to focus on for Landsharks. If given the option, Landsharks should always aim to attack ranged attackers over melee ones. Landsharks do not provoke opportunity attacks, allowing them to swim past the melee line. Thus if they can reach a ranged attacker and attack them they should do so. Otherwise, they will attack the melee attacker closest to them if already in range and then swim away.
system.runningMonster:
A large group of landsharks is a good challenge for a group of adventurers.

As a note, when a player makes a readied action against the Landshark to hit it when it comes up, the readied attack will go off first.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides

system.description: You move underground at your normal speed. You do not provoke attacks of opportunities except from other burrowed creatures.

When not attacking, only a single fin sticks out from under the ground. While you are not attacking, you gain a +10/+20 bonus to your dodge except against other burrowed creatures. You cannot make reactions while not underground.
You leap out from below that ground and make a Heavy attack against the target.

system.biography: Mages are spellcasters without a specialization. They are the most common type of mage, though most will soon specialize in an element or magic type. They exist in every race, though human mages are the rarest ones.

details.appearance: A humanoid creature.
details.habitat: Can be found anywhere.

system.tactics:
Mages prefer to stay in the back, using either Glittershards to block off enemy ranged attackers or using Arcane Net to entrap enemy melee attackers. Possibly both. Afterwards, they will use Missile Barrage to soften up all enemies. Depending on their allies and the battle situation, mages may want to retain some mana to recast the net or glittershards. 

If they are under threat, they will want to reserve 1 mana to make Block a valid option. A mage engaged in melee combat can’t do much, they will have to disengage and move away.
system.runningMonster:
Mages are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being both a ranged controller and AoE striker. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Apprentice’ generic enemy.

Mages can function with Grunt level allies, though they will need to be set up in situations where their control abilities can shine. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Mages generally use a channeling weapon and wear no armor.

system.description: When taking the Block action while you have at least 1 mana, your Guard is increased by an additional 8.

You place a 20x20ft net of arcane energy at a point within range. The net is considered difficult terrain for your enemies. You may spend 0 RP to cancel the net, immediately rooting all creatures within the net’s area of effect at that time until the start of your next turn.

Numerous sparkling arcane crystals swarm the area and block line of sight.  Targets inside of or within 5ft of the Glittershards can only see up to 5ft into or out of Glittershards.  Glittershards lasts for up to 10 minutes and you can only have 1 Glittershards active at a time.  You can end this effect for 0 AP on your turn.
You make a Light attack that deals Arcane damage to all enemies within range.
